messages.author: b063227c9709ab9e
messages.subject: Density estimates and multi-session masks
parts:
Hi there,

I have capture-recapture data for spotted hyaenas and leopards from camera trap surveys which took place over four sampling sessions (two wet and two dry seasons). Each session ran for 60 consecutive nights, however effort/usage for each session differs due to camera trap malfunctions. I have no problem creating the capthist file with different trap detector usages as seen below:

mydetectors <- c("S1_trapfile.csv", "S2_trapfile.csv", "S3_trapfile.csv", "S4_trapfile.csv")

SP_Left <- read.capthist("hyaenaleftcapturehist2.csv", mydetectors, detector = "proximity", fmt = "trapID", 
trapcovnames =c( 'vegetation', 'elevation', 'slope', 'road', 'distancetowater'))

However, I am struggling to determine how to create the mask component of the secr.fit models. Using the game reserve boundary as a mask is not valid as we suspect that both leopards
and hyaenas could be moving in and out of the reserve (despite the reserve being fenced). 

I used a constant mask (SPmask <- make.mask(traps(SP_Left), buffer = 3200, spacing = 1975, type = 'trapbuffer')) across all sessions for spotted hyaena by using MaxDM calculated from three 
collared hyaenas and using the average space between camera traps. The population size estimates for the best fit model according to AIC is as seen below, which is was we expect 
however, R.N gives NA values (which from a previous post I see isn't all bad):

> region.N(secrroad, region=SPmask, se.N=TRUE, aSPha=0.05)
[[1]]
    estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl  n
E.N 40.10309    4.301249 32.51946 49.45525 34
R.N 45.86846         NaN      NaN      NaN 34

[[2]]
    estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl  n
E.N 40.10309    4.301249 32.51946 49.45525 22
R.N 34.63226         NaN      NaN      NaN 22

[[3]]
    estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl  n
E.N 40.10309    4.301249 32.51946 49.45525 32
R.N 43.91056         NaN      NaN      NaN 32

[[4]]
    estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl  n
E.N 40.10309    4.301249 32.51946 49.45525 24
R.N 36.00153         NaN      NaN      NaN 24


If I want to use MMDM per session as the buffer for spotted hyaenas or the RPSV values, firstly would this be correct and secondly how do I go about writing the code to incorporate a list
of values per session in making a mask?

Hope this all makes sense.

Kind regards,
Jess

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Density estimates and multi-session masks
parts:
Hi Jess

I'm not sure I quite get which N you want: is it the number of hyaenas/leopards centred within the reserve boundary? If that is the case then specify that a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame for the boundary as the region argument of region.N() (see ?region.N). If you choose to specify the reserve region as a mask object then use a small pixel size (spacing) so the edge is not too crude. There is no buffer involved here.

Given that you believe there is free movement across the boundary, for model fitting you will want to define a much larger mask using a buffer that is some multiple of sigma (or RPSV(CC=TRUE,...); I don't know why you would mess with a crude statistic like MMDM). Dodging your question - there is no serious argument for making the mask buffer vary across sessions - just make it large enough to work for all sessions. Possibly it needs to be different for hyaenas and leopards, but I doubt it.

Murray

Thank you for your response, all my doubts have been restored and I will use the RPSV(CC=TRUE) value across all my sessions. The RPSV value is slightly larger for leopards.

Jess
